applicable_when: The kernel loads from in_ptr0 with address pattern y0 + 128*x2 + 2032128*y1. Within a warp, threads vary along the XBLOCK dimension (x2), so consecutive threads access addresses 128 floats (512 bytes) apart — a stride-128 access that defeats L1 coalescing and causes every load to miss L1 (2.52% hit rate). The L2 is saturated at 97.1%. Adding tl.max_contiguous and tl.multiple_of hints on the x-dimension index tells the Triton compiler that the access is contiguous and aligned, enabling it to emit 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads instead of scalar 32-bit loads. This reduces the number of memory transactions by 4x for the x-dimension loads, relieves L2 pressure, and reduces L1TEX stall cycles. The store to out_ptr0 already has a contiguous pattern (x2 varies fastest) and benefits similarly from vectorization hints.
